Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you shape this into a useful prompt for drafting two connected pieces for the Lantern Film Society at Bellweather College: a public event page and an internal run-of-show for our autumn screening. i’ve got the details in bits and don’t want the actual page or schedule written yet, just a clear prompt that tells a writer what to make. Keep the pieces consistent with each other, and distinguish what can be stated publicly from what belongs only in the internal plan. We’re trying to make the event welcoming to students who have never come to a repertory screening, while still giving regular members enough practical information.

The event is planned for Saturday, October 24, 2026, in the college’s Calder Hall. Doors are due to open at 6:30 p.m.; the screening is scheduled for 7:00 p.m. and the room must be cleared by 9:45 p.m. The film we are discussing is The Orchard at Dusk, directed by fictional filmmaker Niko Saye. The distributor has not yet confirmed the screening license. If written confirmation arrives by October 9, we can proceed with the title; if it does not, we need to keep the event slot but leave the film title out of the public announcement until the society chooses a cleared alternative. Don’t make it sound as though the license has already been granted, and don’t invent the alternative title. The society has a 110-minute booking window from doors to room clearance, including the film and any introduction or discussion, so the internal schedule needs to fit that window rather than quietly extending it.

Our venue seats 84, with 10 seats that can be reserved for people who request an access accommodation. We expect around 55 attendees based on the last two screenings, but that is an estimate, not a ticket count. Admission is free, and people should reserve a place using the society’s campus form; walk-ins can be admitted only if seats remain. Please say that reservations are recommended without implying they guarantee entry. There is no food service in Calder Hall. The society may offer tea and packaged biscuits in the foyer before the doors open, but that is still dependent on a student volunteer being available, so don’t promise refreshments. The college’s general evening contact desk is staffed until 8:30 p.m.; after that, the society’s event lead, Mara Venn, is the contact for urgent event questions. We don’t have a public phone number for Mara, so the page should direct questions to the society email, lanternfilms@bellweather.example.

Please preserve the following remarks exactly wherever they are used; they came from the people named and should not be rewritten or turned into stronger claims. Society chair Mara Venn said, “We want the room to feel welcoming even if someone has never been to a repertory screening.” Projectionist Eli Rook said, “Please don’t promise a 35 mm print; the distributor has only confirmed the DCP.” Accessibility coordinator Leena Ortiz said, “If the caption file arrives by Tuesday at noon, we can test it before doors.” Keep the names and wording attached to the right people. The distributor’s confirmation is specifically about the DCP format, not the license, so don’t make those sound like the same confirmation.

There are also two short source notes that should stay exactly as written if included: “Distributor confirms DCP only; no 35 mm print.” and “North entrance is step-free; balcony lift is unreliable.” The second note is about the building, not a claim that every route inside the hall is accessible. Calder Hall is on the ground floor, and the north entrance is the step-free entrance. The lift serves the balcony but has been unreliable this term; the screening seats are on the main floor. The accessible washroom is in the adjoining Arts Wing, about a two-minute indoor walk from the hall, and the route is level. Don’t describe the balcony as accessible or promise that the lift will work. For specific access questions, direct readers to lanternfilms@bellweather.example so Leena can reply. We have not yet received a request for an audio-described version, and we don’t know whether one is available, so don’t say that it is.

The caption-file timing needs to be handled carefully. If the file arrives by Tuesday, October 20, at noon, Leena and Eli can test it before doors. If it has not arrived by then, the team should not advertise the screening as captioned and should send a brief update to people who reserved seats. The public wording should not imply that the file is guaranteed to arrive. Do not replace this with a vague promise to “check accessibility.” The internal plan should show who follows up: Leena checks with the distributor on Tuesday morning, and Eli is available for a test from 4:30 to 5:00 p.m. on event day if the file has arrived and is usable. If a test reveals a problem, the plan should say to tell Mara before doors so the society can update attendees; don’t invent a technical fix or state that the captions will work.

For the internal run-of-show, use this sequence as a starting point and keep the timing realistic:
1. 5:45 p.m. Mara and two volunteers arrive; check the hall booking, foyer table, reserved-access seating, and directional signs.
2. 6:00 p.m. Eli checks the DCP playback and sound with the hall technician; this is not a film-license check.
3. 6:30 p.m. Open doors, welcome attendees, and keep the step-free north entrance clear.
4. 6:55 p.m. Mara gives a brief welcome and mentions the society email for follow-up questions.
5. 7:00 p.m. Start the film only if the screening license is confirmed; otherwise the event lead follows the title-contingency plan and the prompt should not assume what the replacement is.
6. After the film, allow at most 10 minutes for optional audience comments, then have volunteers clear the room by 9:45 p.m.
The film runtime is listed as 94 minutes. Don’t add a long director introduction, a formal Q&A, or an intermission; none has been arranged. A volunteer named Jo Pell is assigned to count attendance at the door without collecting names. Another volunteer, Sanjay Bell, manages the foyer and makes sure the entrance stays clear. The event lead has to confirm the room is empty before leaving, but no one has assigned a specific person to lock the hall.

The society’s available event budget is $180. The hall booking costs $60, and the distributor license fee, if the screening is confirmed, is $75. The remaining amount is for printing signs and possible foyer tea and biscuits; don’t allocate a precise amount to those items because prices have not been checked. We have 30 reusable seat-reservation cards and 40 printed directional arrows from last term. The printer in the student union can make another batch, but the society has not asked for a quote. The public page may mention that the screening is free, but the budget breakdown and volunteer assignments belong in the internal run-of-show, not the public copy. Don’t imply that the $180 has already been spent.

The public page should be friendly, clear, and fairly compact, with the date, venue, door and start times, film title only under the license condition above, reservation details, and the known access information. Explain that the event is open to Bellweather students and staff; guests may attend with a student or staff host, subject to available seats. Avoid promising refreshments, caption availability, a particular print format, or a guaranteed seat. The internal run-of-show should make the dependencies and handoffs easy to scan, retain the named responsibilities, and fit the available booking window. Keep the quoted remarks and the two source notes verbatim if you use them, and do not turn internal uncertainty into a public certainty. End the prompt by asking the writer to return both pieces with clear labels, not by asking them to decide the unresolved license, caption, or refreshment questions.", "output": "Draft two connected pieces for the Lantern Film Society at Bellweather College’s autumn screening: a public event page and an internal run-of-show. Keep them consistent, but distinguish public information from internal planning. The aim is to welcome students who are new to repertory screenings while giving regular attendees practical details. Return both pieces with clear labels. Do not write conclusions about unresolved matters or decide them on the society’s behalf.

## Event details and dependencies

The screening is planned for Saturday, October 24, 2026, in Calder Hall. Doors open at 6:30 p.m., the film is scheduled to start at 7:00 p.m., and the room must be cleared by 9:45 p.m. The 110-minute booking window runs from doors opening to room clearance and must include the film and any introduction or discussion. The film, *The Orchard at Dusk*, is directed by fictional filmmaker Niko Saye. Its screening license is not yet confirmed. If written confirmation arrives by October 9, the society can proceed with that title. If it does not, keep the event slot but omit the film title from the public announcement until the society selects a cleared alternative. Do not invent an alternative or imply that the license has been granted.

The distributor has confirmed the DCP format, not the license. Preserve this distinction. If used, retain this source note exactly: “Distributor confirms DCP only; no 35 mm print.” Do not promise a 35 mm print or conflate format confirmation with licensing.

The film runtime is 94 minutes. Do not add a long director introduction, formal Q&A, or intermission; none has been arranged. An optional audience-comment period after the film may last no more than 10 minutes. The plan must still fit the booking window.

## Public event page

Use a friendly, clear, fairly compact style. Include the event date, venue, door and start times, reservation information, and known access details. Include the film title only if the license condition above is met. The event is open to Bellweather students and staff; guests may attend with a student or staff host, subject to available seats.

Admission is free. Attendees should reserve a place using the society’s campus form; walk-ins may be admitted only if seats remain. Say that reservations are recommended, not that they guarantee entry. Calder Hall seats 84, including 10 seats that can be reserved for people requesting an access accommodation. About 55 attendees are expected based on the last two screenings, but this is an estimate, not a ticket count.

Calder Hall is on the ground floor. Its north entrance is step-free, and screening seats are on the main floor. The accessible washroom is in the adjoining Arts Wing, about a two-minute indoor walk away along a level route. The balcony lift has been unreliable this term; do not describe the balcony as accessible or promise the lift will work. If used, retain this source note exactly: “North entrance is step-free; balcony lift is unreliable.” For specific access questions, direct readers to lanternfilms@bellweather.example so accessibility coordinator Leena Ortiz can reply. No request for an audio-described version has been received, and its availability is unknown; do not claim one is available.

Do not promise refreshments. The society may offer tea and packaged biscuits in the foyer before doors open, but this depends on a student volunteer being available. There is no food service in Calder Hall. The college’s general evening contact desk is staffed until 8:30 p.m. After that, event lead Mara Venn is the contact for urgent event questions. No public phone number for Mara is available, so direct questions to lanternfilms@bellweather.example.

## Exact remarks

If you use these remarks, preserve each one exactly and keep it attached to the correct person. Do not turn them into stronger claims.

- Society chair Mara Venn: “We want the room to feel welcoming even if someone has never been to a repertory screening.”
- Projectionist Eli Rook: “Please don’t promise a 35 mm print; the distributor has only confirmed the DCP.”
- Accessibility coordinator Leena Ortiz: “If the caption file arrives by Tuesday at noon, we can test it before doors.”

## Caption-file contingency

If the caption file arrives by Tuesday, October 20, at noon, Leena and Eli can test it before doors. If it has not arrived by then, do not advertise the screening as captioned and have the team send a brief update to people who reserved seats. Public wording must not imply that the file is guaranteed to arrive, and this contingency must not be reduced to a vague promise to “check accessibility.”

Leena checks with the distributor on Tuesday morning. If the file has arrived and is usable, Eli is available to test it on event day from 4:30 to 5:00 p.m. If a test reveals a problem, the plan should tell Mara before doors so the society can update attendees. Do not invent a technical fix or state that captions will work.

## Internal run-of-show

Use this sequence as the starting point. Keep all timings realistic and within the booking window:

1. **5:45 p.m.** Mara and two volunteers arrive. Check the hall booking, foyer table, reserved-access seating, and directional signs.
2. **6:00 p.m.** Eli checks DCP playback and sound with the hall technician. This is not a film-license check.
3. **6:30 p.m.** Open doors, welcome attendees, and keep the step-free north entrance clear.
4. **6:55 p.m.** Mara gives a brief welcome and mentions the society email for follow-up questions.
5. **7:00 p.m.** Start the film only if the screening license is confirmed. Otherwise, the event lead follows the title-contingency plan; do not assume or invent the replacement title.
6. **After the film.** Allow at most 10 minutes for optional audience comments, then have volunteers clear the room by 9:45 p.m.

Jo Pell counts attendees at the door without collecting names. Sanjay Bell manages the foyer and keeps the entrance clear. The event lead confirms the room is empty before leaving. No one has been assigned to lock the hall, so do not assign a person to that task.

## Budget and materials

The available event budget is $180. The hall booking costs $60. If the screening is confirmed, the distributor license fee is $75. The remaining amount is for printing signs and possible foyer tea and biscuits; prices have not been checked, so do not assign precise amounts to those items. The society has 30 reusable seat-reservation cards and 40 printed directional arrows from last term. The student-union printer can make another batch, but the society has not requested a quote.
